newsitem.title: USA: White House's Stiglitz sees strong Q4 growth.
newsitem.headline: White House's Stiglitz sees strong Q4 growth.

text.p: White House chief economist Joseph Stiglitz said Friday he expects strong economic growth in the fourth quarter and into 1997.
"The economy is likely to have strong growth going forward into the next quarter and into 1997," he told reporters at a pre-election briefing on the economy.
Stiglitz, who heads the Council of Economic Advisers, said he expects "very strong consumer demand" in the fourth quarter as personal income continues to rise and confidence is high.
The economy grew at a 2.2 percent annualized pace in the third quarter after 4.7 percent growth in the second.
Stiglitz said that the economy this year is "doing stronger" than the administration has forecast. The administration forecast growth this year of 2.6 percent.
Stiglitz and other senior administration officials briefed reporters following news today that the unemployment rate held steady at 5.2 percent in October as the economy created 210,000 jobs.
"I feel confident that we will be able to maintain the kinds of low unemployment rates that we have in the mid fives (percent) without any threat of inflationary pressures," Stiglitz said.
